By default, NATS waits up to 10 seconds for the `nats-server` to send the initial "ready" signal [1]. To extend this default time, set the `NATS_STARTUP_DELAY` environment variable to a suitable duration, such as "30s" for 30 seconds [1].

NATS clients shuffle the server list on reconnect to prevent a _thundering herd_ situation where all clients try to reconnect to the same server immediately, causing a denial of service attack [4]. This shuffling does matter if you only configure one server, as there is no server to shuffle from or to.

To confirm that the server has received published messages, a client uses [PING/PONG interaction] (connecting/pingpong.md) built into the NATS protocol. When an application calls flush, most libraries will put a PING on the outgoing queue of messages and wait for the server to respond with a PONG before saying that the flush was successful. [1][2]

[1] states that even though the client uses PING/PONG for flush, pings sent this way do not count towards [max outgoing pings](connecting/pingpong.md). [2] also mentions this, stating that pings sent for flush do not count towards [max outgoing pings](connecting/pingpong.md) as well.

This shuffling does matter if you configure only one server, as there would be no randomization, and all clients would attempt to connect to that single server, potentially overwhelming it [4].
